title: Caste Row Erupts After Purification Ritual at Kharge Rally Venue in Haldwani
excerpt: Congress accused a right-wing group of performing shuddhikaran because Kharge is a Dalit, while the BJP denied any caste motive and blamed anti-Sanatan slogans raised at the rally.
body:
• A right-wing group called Shri Ram Sena performed a shuddhikaran (purification) ceremony at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge held a rally there on August 8.
  • Congress accused the BJP-affiliated group of targeting the venue because Kharge belongs to the Dalit community, calling it a "crime against humanity."
  • The BJP denied any ties to the group and said the ceremony was prompted by slogans at the rally that offended Sanatan religious sentiments.

A political firestorm has erupted in Uttarakhand after a group calling itself the Shri Ram Sena performed a shuddhikaran — or purification ceremony — at the Ramlila Ground in Haldwani following a rally addressed by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on August 8. The incident has triggered a sharp clash between the Congress and the BJP over caste, religion, and political motives.

Uttarakhand Congress chief Ganesh Godiyal alleged that the purification ritual was conducted because Kharge belongs to the Dalit community, and accused the group of being affiliated with the BJP. He described the act as a "crime against humanity" and said it highlighted the "fundamental difference in ideology between the Congress and the BJP," according to The Economic Times.

Congress Demands Police Action

Godiyal questioned why the Nainital senior superintendent of police had not taken action against the group. He accused the BJP of creating social divisions in the name of caste, framing the incident as evidence of entrenched discrimination that persists despite constitutional protections against untouchability.

The Congress party's position was echoed in reports across multiple outlets. The Times of India reported that Kharge raised the matter in the Rajya Sabha, stating, "You treat me as untouchable." NDTV reported that Kharge described the purification ritual as being "against Hindu religion" itself — arguing that the act of ritually cleansing a venue after a Dalit leader's visit violates the inclusive principles of Hinduism.

BJP Denies Caste Motive

The BJP vehemently denied any organizational link to the Shri Ram Sena. BJP state spokesperson and Cabinet Minister Khajan Das offered a different explanation for the ceremony, claiming that certain slogans were raised during Kharge's rally that hurt the sentiments of the Sanatan community. Das said the Ramlila Ground is a place of religious significance, and that people were angered by the chanting of slogans associated with another religion at the venue, according to The Economic Times.

The BJP also dismissed the Congress's framing of the incident as caste-based discrimination. Das accused the Congress of disrespecting its own Dalit leaders historically, citing the treatment of former Congress presidents Sitaram Kesri and Babu Jagjivan Ram, as well as B.R. Ambedkar.

Wider Context of Caste Politics

The confrontation comes against the backdrop of an increasingly charged debate over caste in Indian politics. Kharge, who is 84, is one of the most prominent Dalit leaders in the country and was elected Congress president in October 2022. His elevation was seen as a signal of the party's commitment to social justice politics — a theme the Congress has sharpened under Rahul Gandhi's push for a nationwide caste census and expanded reservations.

The shuddhikaran controversy also follows a broader pattern of such incidents across India. In April 2025, a BJP leader in another state drew national attention for performing a similar purification ritual at a temple after Dalit community members entered to offer prayers during Ram Navami. Such episodes regularly surface in Indian public life, spotlighting the gap between constitutional abolition of untouchability and its persistence in social practice.

Parliamentary Fallout

The row has spilled into Parliament during what has been a turbulent monsoon session. The Rajya Sabha, where Kharge serves as Leader of the Opposition, has seen repeated confrontations between the ruling party and the opposition over issues ranging from the delimitation bill to examination reforms. The Haldwani purification incident has added fuel to what was already a deeply polarized session, with both sides using the controversy to mobilize their respective bases ahead of upcoming state elections.
